features.label: Features overview
features.tagline: What WinProx does — in plain language
features.highlight: One app: someone reports an issue, a team gets a task, the work is closed. The punch clock is included.
features.intro: WinProx is a Facility app for locations, units and teams. No separate contractor or hospitality portals. Time (punch clock) is included in every plan.
features.source: The same content as the in-app manual and FAQ.
features.footer_right: See also: Technical fact sheet (hosting, GDPR, security)

full.title: Issues
full.body: Someone spots a problem and creates an issue — via the unit QR, in admin, or from a sensor (IoT).
items: Filters and approval of QR issues.
Optional contact details or email confirmation for anonymous reporters.
Public QR pages show it only after approval; admin sees everything at once.
A Reporter confirmed pill after the email link is confirmed.
Recurring maintenance can be paused or closed.

full.title: Tasks
full.body: One issue can have several tasks. Each task goes to one team.
items: Priority, deadline and notes per task.
Follow-up in the task list and via QR on site.

full.title: Close-out
full.body: The team finishes the tasks. When everything is done, admin closes the issue.
items: Optional photo and note when completing.
Status and history in admin.
Workers use the unit QR, or Clock Point with an open GPS work visit.

full.title: Dashboard
full.body: The home screen shows what is still open. Click a card to open that list.
items: Locations, units, new issues and open tasks.
With Time: who is present now.
Pending leave or TOIL as an extra card: 1 Leave, 1 TOIL, or both.
New organisations can pick a starter template here.
Briefing and reports are available from the dashboard.

full.title: Facility
full.body: This is where you set up places, people and teams.
items: Categories, locations and units (including bulk or CSV).
Documents and announcements on the portal.
Find workers under People → Workers; optional portrait.
Floater teams may clock in anywhere; others only at assigned sites.
Rare actions (team leader, icon, phone, PIN) live in Edit, not in the list.

full.title: QR portals
full.body: Everything opens in the browser. No App Store.
items: Unit QR: report issues, optional unit check and measurements.
Clock Point QR: sign in (name + icon) and team tasks; clock-in only with Time.
Printable as sticker sheets or A6/A5/A4.
A loaded unit QR stays usable offline; clock-in needs a fresh scan.
Optional: Clock Point link on the phone home screen.

full.title: Unit checks
full.body: Quickly say a unit is fine — for example after a round.
items: On the unit QR: OK or Not OK.
OK does not need a separate issue.
Optional checklist, note and up to 4 photos.
History under Work → Unit checks.

full.title: Inspection rounds
full.body: A fixed route of units, even across sites.
items: Plan under Work → Inspection rounds.
Per stop: OK, Not OK (with an issue) or skip with a reason.
With Time + GPS, today’s round appears under Where should I go today.
Print a cycle from the round task.

full.title: Unit measurements
full.body: Simple readings on a unit, without the ESG module.
items: Mileage, temperature, status, and so on.
Fields under Work → Unit measurements; enable per category and unit.
Via QR or API; webhook unit.measurement.recorded.

full.title: Photos
full.body: Photos are compressed on the device before upload.
items: Up to 4 photos on an issue, close-out or unit check.
Up to 4 unit photos and a background per unit.
Reporter photos on the public portal only after approval.

full.title: GPS
full.body: For mobile units (vehicle, machine) you can store a location.
items: Enable per category.
History in admin; open in Maps.

full.title: Time
full.body: Time is the punch clock. Workers clock in and out on the same Clock Point QR they use for field work.
items: Each clock-in or clock-out needs a fresh QR scan on site.
Included in the trial and in every plan.
Presence, timesheets and My hours (own shifts only).
Staff can clock someone in by hand if the phone was forgotten.
CIAO (NSSO) on request, at no extra fee.
Optional GPS work visits: Start work on the site pin.

full.title: Roster
full.body: Staff plan shifts under Time → Roster. Publishing shows them on Clock Point, not at the NSSO.
items: Type a code or a free time such as 07:00-15:00.
Week or month view; weekends can be hidden.
Clock Point shows My roster (own published shifts only).
A red triangle if you have not clocked in or are late.
Admin sees planned versus clocked (15-minute window).

full.title: Leave and TOIL
full.body: Workers request leave or time off in lieu on Clock Point. Staff decide under Time → Requests.
items: From–to, max. 31 days, not in the past.
Reject needs a reason; approve does not.
On approval WinProx stores existing duties, then replaces them on the roster.
No email and no sick-leave request in this step.
The dashboard shows 1 Leave, 1 TOIL, or both.

full.title: Calendar
full.body: Month, week and day views of tasks, issues and reservations.
items: Print that day’s briefing from the calendar.

full.title: Briefing
full.body: A printable list of open tasks for the chosen day, grouped by team.
items: Available from Dashboard, Tasks and Calendar.

full.title: Reports
full.body: On search screens you can export the filtered list.
items: CSV for Excel, or print to PDF.
Same filters as the list (max. 5,000 rows).
Time shows a timesheet.

full.title: Reservations
full.body: For shared assets with a time slot, such as a room or vehicle.
items: Reservable category + Reservations allowed on the unit.
Guests book via the unit QR (email confirmation).

full.title: ESG & Compliance
full.body: Readings for environment, safety and compliance — next to everyday tasks.
items: Indicators, measurements and follow-up tasks.
Via portal, admin or API.

full.title: IoT Connect
full.body: Sensors send events. An alarm becomes an approved issue with a task.
items: Readings can feed ESG.
Separate gateway token, even without the full REST API.

full.title: API & webhooks
full.body: Other software can use the same data WinProx uses.
items: Tokens and outbound webhooks under Settings → API.
See the API & Webhooks and Technical sheets.

full.title: Multi-tenant
full.body: Each organisation has its own environment, with limits per plan.
items: A licence is a colleague with login or a worker. Colleague + punch clock counts as one.
Units and documents = 5× licences. Locations and photos are unlimited.

full.title: Branding & QR
full.body: You can make the portal look like your organisation.
items: Logo, background and button colours under Settings.
Stickers: Avery or A6/A5/A4.

full.title: Work menu
full.body: Admin chooses which extras appear in the sidebar.
items: Calendar, Reservations, Inspection rounds and Unit measurements per organisation.
Off = no admin access; existing unit QR still works.

full.title: AI translation
full.body: After approval WinProx queues texts for translation.
items: Local AI, no external AI cloud.
Usually daily, with no fixed turnaround.
Admins can correct translations themselves.

full.title: No app needed
full.body: Everything in the browser. Admin on a laptop; field and QR on the phone.
items: No App Store.
Optional Clock Point shortcut on the home screen.

full.title: Roles
full.body: Four roles, no extra portals.
items: Administrator: everything, including billing.
Staff: day-to-day follow-up, no billing.
Worker: field work via Clock Point and unit QR, no login.
Team leader: release icons and coordinate via Clock Point.

full.title: Admin sign-in
full.body: Colleagues sign in with email and password, or Sign in with Microsoft.
items: Existing WinProx accounts only; the email must match.
Workers stay on Clock Point (name + icon).
Other software connects with API keys, not this login.

technical.label: Technical fact sheet
technical.tagline: Facility issues: QR → tasks → completion · SaaS for operational teams
technical.intro: Overview for IT and security. WinProx is a multi-tenant web app (Laravel + MySQL). Each customer organisation has its own isolated environment.
technical.footer_left: WinProx · info@winprox.app · Product overview, not legal advice or an SLA.
technical.footer_right: Questions? We are happy to walk through the DPA, subprocessors and integrations.

left.title: Hosting
items: Production on **Linux** (EU), at **Cloud86**.
Access via **HTTPS** (encrypted connection, TLS).
Stack: PHP 8.2+, Laravel 12, Livewire, MySQL, Vite frontend.
Email via SMTP in the EU; billing by yearly invoice (no online checkout). Only WinProx (Superuser) assigns the plan; organisations do not self-select a subscription.
Pricing: from **€7 / seat / month** (10 seats + 50 units), **€6** (25 + 125), **€5** (50 + 250). Billed yearly by invoice. Corporate is custom.

left.title: Backups
items: Automatic **daily** backups via Cloud86 (files + database), retained for **7 days**.
**RPO ≈ 24 hours**: in the worst case you lose data since the last nightly backup (Recovery Point Objective = max. acceptable data loss).
**RTO: best effort, typically within 1 business day** (Recovery Time Objective = time until the service is available again after restore).
On full organisation deletion: separate technical SQL snapshot **without media**, max. **30 days** (not the same as a disaster-recovery backup).

left.title: Database
items: **MySQL**, relational model per tenant.
Strict **tenant isolation**: every query/API call stays within the organisation.
No shared visibility between customers.
**Location scope:** pivot tables location_user and location_worker; teams.clocks_all_locations for floaters; workers.user_id links colleague to worker profile.

left.title: Permissions
items: **Admin**: everything (users, company, subscription, teams).
**Employee**: operational (issues, tasks, locations) — no account/billing management.
**Worker / team leader**: complete tasks via the field portal; team leaders can release icons and a bound phone.
Every action is checked: you only get what your role allows (**least privilege**). API keys get separate permissions — e.g. “read issues” without access to everything.

Operational reports: filtered CSV or print on issues, tasks, Time, reservations, unit checks, unit measurements and ESG — for users who may view those lists. Print follows the list layout where possible; Time = timesheet. Separate from the GDPR account export (Settings → Privacy & data export).

Work menu: tenant columns work_menu_*_enabled; sidebar and backoffice routes via TenantWorkMenuAccess; starter template sets defaults via UpdateTenantWorkMenuAction (removing template does not revert menu).

left.title: API
items: **REST API v1** (fixed URLs + HTTP methods) with **JSON** responses (standard data format). Documentation in-app + docs.
Incl. issues, tasks, locations, units (incl. external ID), teams, workers, unit check (also inbound via external unit ID), unit measurements, ESG, translations.
Available on **Corporate** (trial on request).
IoT ingest separately via gateway token (Corporate).

right.title: GDPR
items: **Customer = controller**; WinProx = **processor**.
Framework: EU GDPR + Belgian Act of 30 July 2018.
Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and subprocessor list available.
Data export (account), self-service organisation deletion, retention periods documented.

Data stays in the **EU** (hosting/email). Stripe EU/US when paying. With **Sign in with Microsoft**, the user is sent to Microsoft Entra ID (Microsoft, EU/US); WinProx receives email (and possibly name) to match the existing account.

Optional email confirmation for QR reports: temporary draft storage until the link; unverified drafts are deleted automatically (typically 60 minutes, including photos). The confirmation mail is only sent to a valid address that is not marked undeliverable (bounce). Unsubscribing from marketing mail does not block this confirmation. No user account.

Optional **CIAO** forwarding (RSZ Check In and Out): when enabled, WinProx stores NISS (encrypted) and sends presence registrations to the **Belgian NSSO/RSZ** (public authority / customer legal duty). RSZ is not a WinProx marketing sub-processor; transfer is for compliance. WinProx uses its own Chaman credentials; the customer only enters the enterprise number. An applied team break on the timesheet is not an extra RSZ IN/OUT. With GPS work visits: clock in/out are not sent to the NSSO; visit start = IN, visit end = OUT. Breaks during a visit remain OUT/IN. Successful submissions older than 12 months (configurable) are deleted automatically; Time → CIAO offers CSV/print export (no SSIN).

Optional planned roster: shifts and absences (leave, time off in lieu, sick) entered by the customer; Clock Point shows only the worker’s own published roster. Sick codes are the customer’s choice; WinProx stores them as processor.

right.title: Availability
items: Available 24/7 as SaaS (browser + QR portals).

Unit QR: a loaded page stays usable without network for tasks, reports and unit checks; it syncs when connectivity returns. Clock Point punches stay online and need a fresh QR scan. Optional home-screen shortcut (per Clock Point, off by default) opens the same URL; no extra offline.
Planned maintenance preferably outside business hours, with notice where possible.
Formal uptime SLA: available contractually on request.

right.title: Authentication
items: Back office: email + password (stored hashed), sessions.

Self-service sign-up requires **email verification**: the account only works after clicking the link in the confirmation mail. The confirmation mail is only sent to a valid address that is not marked undeliverable (bounce). Unsubscribing from marketing mail does not block this confirmation. Unverified sign-ups are automatically and completely deleted after 7 days.

**SSO** (one work login via Microsoft Entra): for admins and employees on desktop (**Sign in with Microsoft**). Only existing WinProx accounts (email must match the Microsoft account); email + password still works. No automatic new accounts. Workers stay on Clock Point QR (name + icon). Connecting other software (Ultimo, IWMS, …) uses API tokens, not SSO.
API: personal **access key** (Bearer token via Laravel Sanctum). Revocable; with scopes = which actions the key may perform.

Workers: **no email login** — Clock Point QR + name + personal icon (or optional PIN). One phone per worker; the icon is hidden after sign-in. Optional Clock Point link on phone home screen (off by default) for field workers who cannot scan a QR.
Offline field actions on the unit QR go through POST /portal/field-sync with the device cookie (no API token). The same client_id does not create a duplicate issue or task change.
Reporters: public QR portal without an account. Optional mailbox proof (category and unit): no login; the issue is created only after the link in the mail.
Colleague with **punch-clock team** gets a linked worker profile for Clock Point (name + icon); does not count twice towards the licence.

right.title: Security
items: HTTPS; hashed passwords; revocable API tokens.
**CSRF protection**: prevents another website from secretly performing actions as a logged-in user.
Tenant scoping; audit/activity logs.
Webhooks with **HMAC-SHA256** signature (proof the message comes from WinProx).
API: max. **60 requests/minute** per token.
Support access: exceptional, read-only by default.

Time Clock Point: a fresh QR scan per clock-in, clock-out or move (an open tab/poll is not enough). One phone per worker (refuse + audit on another device). There is no switch-worker control (including on the icon/PIN step) and after sign-in the Sign in heading is hidden; Sign out returns to icon/PIN without clocking out, and the phone stays bound until an admin or team leader releases it. Optional hashed PIN and GPS (punch proceeds without a signal). API clock-in does not bind a phone. Manual clock-in in back office (admin/staff) does not bind a phone. My hours (tile after sign-in): only the signed-in worker’s own shifts. My roster: only that worker’s published roster for the month. A red triangle marks a published work shift without clock-in or at least 15 minutes late. A warning if GPS is off on the phone, only when there are destinations today. Evacuation list (optional in Settings, off by default; tile after sign-in): names only after confirming the consultation is exceptional; each view is logged (first name, last name, date and time). Views from today light up Time attention on the dashboard and on Presence. Time → Alarms keeps the full list (date and time, newest first). Admins release phone, PIN and icon via People → Teams → Edit. During an open work visit Clock Point shows the current location and next stop at the top. Today locations follow inspection-round stop order. Clock Point stores an essential device cookie (about 1 year). An applied team break on the timesheet is not an RSZ/CIAO event (no fake IN/OUT). GPS work visits: fresh GPS at click time (maximumAge 0) to start/stop work on a location pin or unit pin; clock-in stays without a GPS gate. After clock-in (GPS work visits on): Today card with planned destinations and Navigate (Google Maps); Start work only on site. With an open visit: start/complete team tasks on Clock Point; next inspection stop (unit check) on site. Optional home-screen shortcut only when the Clock Point checkbox is on (off by default; not for TFT screens with rotating QR).

right.title: Webhooks
items: Outbound HTTP POST on events (incl. issue/task status, unit check, unit measurement, ESG, GPS, Time/CIAO). time.visit.started / time.visit.ended.
Configured under Settings → API; secret for verification.
Automatic retries on failure (several attempts with increasing delay).
Same plan requirement as API (Corporate).
With optional email confirmation, the **issue created** event fires only after the link, not when the form is submitted on the portal.

full.title: Spam & abuse (limits)
items: **Public QR issues** (per device/IP, per unit): max. **1 issue per 3 minutes**; max. **5 issues per 30 minutes** on the same unit; max. **20 issues per hour** across all units of the same organisation. (Signed-in workers are exempt.)
**Worker sign-in (icon)**: after **2 wrong icon choices** the worker is locked until a team leader or admin releases them.
**Back-office login** (email/password): passwords hashed; no separate app rate limit on failed logins (can be strengthened via infra/contract).

Extra: QR issues on the public portal stay **invisible until approval**. Optional email confirmation (category and unit) holds the report until the email link; existing QR limits count at submit. API has its own rate limit (60/min).

full.title: AI (Artificial Intelligence)
items: After approval, operational texts (issues, tasks, units, announcements, …) are queued for AI translation.
Assistant knowledge base answers (superuser) use the same Ollama pipeline as operational content.
Runs on a **local Ollama instance** — no ChatGPT / external AI cloud for this feature.
WinProx runs translations **periodically** (typically daily), **with no guaranteed turnaround**. Organisation admins can **correct translations manually**. No per-organisation on/off switch.
No generative “AI assistant” that autonomously decides customer processes — translation is support, not decision-making.

full.title: Time: leave and TOIL
items: Workers request leave or time off in lieu on Clock Point (from–to, max. 31 days).
Staff decide under Time → Requests. Reject needs a reason; approve does not.
Approval stores existing roster cells on the request, then replaces them.
No email, no write REST API. Events: time.absence.requested|cancelled|approved|rejected.
The dashboard shows pending requests per kind (1 Leave, 1 TOIL, or both).

api_webhooks.label: API & Webhooks
api_webhooks.tagline: Integrate WinProx with your existing software via APIs and webhooks.
api_webhooks.highlight: WinProx is not a replacement for existing IWMS or ERP systems. Thanks to APIs and webhooks, WinProx works alongside them.
api_webhooks.intro: WinProx is built so other software can use the same data, issues, tasks and unit checks as WinProx itself. Admin and docs live under Settings → API. Desktop Sign in with Microsoft is not an API link: other software uses tokens, not SSO. Leave and TOIL requests have time.absence.* events (no write REST API in this slice).
api_webhooks.footer_right: See also: Features overview · Technical fact sheet

left.title: Why APIs and webhooks?
left.body: With the API and webhooks, WinProx can work with existing software. For example:
items: automatically forward an issue to your IWMS, CMMS or ERP;
forward a unit check (OK/Not OK) to your external facility software;
record a unit measurement (POST /units/{unit}/measurements);
receive a unit check from your external facility software (via external unit ID);
synchronise tasks with an ERP system;
show data in Power BI;
let IoT sensors create issues automatically;
connect to your own software or Microsoft Power Automate.
left.emphasis: Your central system (IWMS, ERP, BI) stays in the lead — WinProx complements it on the shop floor.

rows: Your system asks WinProx for something
WinProx sends a message to your system

left.title: What this is not
items: Not every action is available via the API. Some parts are intentionally read-only or support only specific actions. That keeps integrations safe and manageable.
You manage webhooks in the app, not via the API.
A generic inbound webhook endpoint for arbitrary external systems is not a product feature yet (IoT and Stripe have their own paths).
API & outbound webhooks: Corporate (trial API on request).

right.title: REST API
right.body: The API lets other software safely retrieve data or perform actions inside WinProx. Communication uses standard REST endpoints and JSON.
items: **Access:** personal access token (Bearer). Revocable. Per token you choose permissions (scopes), e.g. read issues only.
**Organisation boundary:** each token belongs to one organisation; you never see another customer’s data.
**Safety:** request rate limit per minute. Optional Idempotency-Key so a repeated request does not create a duplicate action.
**IoT separately:** sensors use a gateway token (Corporate), not the same API token.

rows: Issues, Tasks, Locations, Units, Teams, Workers, Unit checks, Unit measurements

Clock in/out, shifts (API clock-in does not bind a phone); release bound device; manual clock-in (POST /api/v1/time/manual-clock-in, admin source, does not bind a phone); apply minimum break (POST /api/v1/time/work-shifts/{id}/apply-required-break); teams expose required_break_minutes; GPS work visits POST /api/v1/time/work-visits/start (unit_id or location_id) and .../end (time:write); webhooks time.visit.started / time.visit.ended

right.title: Outbound webhooks
right.body: WinProx sends an HTTP POST to a URL you provide whenever something happens.
items: **Setup:** Settings → API → Webhooks (URL + which events). The secret is shown once — store it safely.
**Proof of origin:** each message has an HMAC signature (verifiable with your secret).
**Reliability:** if delivery fails, WinProx retries (with increasing delay). Deliveries appear in a log.

**Other events include:** issue created / approved / status changed · task created / started / completed · Time (incl. CIAO presence) · GPS · ESG · reservations · test button · unit check recorded. With email confirmation: **issue created** only after the link. time.visit.started / time.visit.ended.
right.emphasis: Example: a worker completes a task. WinProx automatically sends a webhook to your external system (IWMS, CMMS or ERP) so a work order can be updated immediately.

full.title: Ready for integration
full.body: WinProx is designed to work alongside existing systems. Suitable for integration with, among others:
items: IWMS / facility management
CMMS / maintenance systems
ERP
Microsoft Power Automate
Power BI
Custom software
IoT platforms
full.emphasis: Have an existing IT landscape? We are happy to explore how WinProx fits. Contact: info@winprox.app · Documentation: Settings → API → Docs
